params.name: eff
params.let: 'the graph keeps that direction' if a > 0 else 'the graph is turned upside down'

stem: Which description matches the graph of $y = {=a}\cdot {=b}^x {=qs} {=qa}$?

choices.correct: It {=dw} as $x$ increases, has the horizontal asymptote $y={=q}$ and cuts the $y$-axis at $(0, {=a+q})$.

distractors.text: It {=dx} as $x$ increases, has the horizontal asymptote $y={=q}$ and cuts the $y$-axis at $(0, {=a+q})$.
It rises as $x$ increases, has the horizontal asymptote $y={=q}$ and cuts the $y$-axis at $(0, {=1+q})$.
It {=dw} as $x$ increases, has the horizontal asymptote $y={=q}$ and cuts the $y$-axis at $(0, {=a})$.
It {=dw} as $x$ increases, has the horizontal asymptote $y=0$ and cuts the $y$-axis at $(0, {=a+q})$.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Takes the x-axis as the asymptote whatever q is
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student treats $y=0$ as the horizontal asymptote of $y=ab^x+q$ and does not move it to $y=q$, so the asymptote is read from the shape $b^x$ alone and the number $q$ is only used, if at all, for the intercept.

solution: Compare $y = {=a}\cdot {=b}^x {=qs} {=qa}$ with $y = a\cdot b^x + q$: here $a = {=a}$, $b = {=b}$ and $q = {=q}$.
Direction: the base $b = {=b}$ is greater than 1, so $b^x$ rises as $x$ increases. Since $a = {=a}$ is {=sg}, {=eff}: it {=dw} as $x$ increases.
Asymptote: as $x$ becomes very negative, $b^x$ gets closer and closer to 0, so $y$ gets closer and closer to $q$. The horizontal asymptote is $y={=q}$.
$y$-intercept: let $x=0$. Then $y = {=a}\cdot {=b}^0 {=qs} {=qa} = {=a}\cdot 1 {=qs} {=qa} = {=a+q}$, so the graph cuts the $y$-axis at $(0, {=a+q})$.
The graph {=dw} as $x$ increases, has the horizontal asymptote $y={=q}$ and cuts the $y$-axis at $(0, {=a+q})$. That is the matching description.
notes: The book's questions in this objective match an equation to one of four printed graphs; a generated family has no figure, so the same skill is asked in words: the student reads the sign of a, the value of q and the y-intercept from the equation and picks the description of the curve. Base greater than 1 only, so the direction is set by the sign of a alone; the base below 1 and the twist it brings are in the advanced family twist. The y-intercept is a + q, never the number in front of the power, and the asymptote is y = q. Every distractor is one catalogued or declared error, and every option is a drawable curve (|q| < |a| puts the point (0, a) and the y-intercept on the side of the line each option needs); the five options are always distinct (q != 0, a != 1, a != 1 + q). Checked by enumerating all 108 valid parameter sets: every correct option matches the numerically computed direction, asymptote and y-intercept, and every distractor differs from it in at least one.
